click **Show all insights** from the risk insights section.

old_evidence.text: The risk insights feature, available with Stripe Radar for Fraud Teams
The data used to populate fraud factor numbers and top fraud factors is only populated for charges made within the last 6 months.
This feature isn’t supported for payments in _sandboxes_
A fraud factor of 3.5x means that charges with a similar value for this risk factor are 3.5 times more likely to be fraudulent than average.

findings: Both snapshots describe Radar using network data and hundreds of risk factors to determine each payment's risk score and level and help decide when to block or send to review. The merchant can open Show all insights. Both say data is retained for up to six months and that older transactions cannot open the interface.

Both say integration-provided email, IP and shipping help Radar compute the available data. Risk insights can show name/email correspondence, transactions' authorization rate on Stripe network associated with the email, and billing/shipping/IP geography. A low rate only might indicate suspicion, because past declines sometimes suggest fraud attempts.

Both dedicated Risk Insights pins say Related Payments includes the merchant's own other payments sharing customer ID, IP, or card number. Many cards sharing one IP or customers sharing a card are possible investigative signals, not fraud verdicts.
substantive_changes: November abbreviates the eligibility and fraud-factor documentation. It omits the earlier Fraud Teams availability attribution, the detailed numbers and Top Fraud Factors sections, hover distribution context and the sandbox statement. Preserve the May scope as historical evidence. Omission establishes no rollout or feature removal.
November still routes users to Show all insights, moved higher on the page, and retains the six-month risk-insights interface restriction.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 10 states availability with Radar for Fraud Teams and describes fraud factor numbers and top factors with a preceding scope of charges within the last six months and no support for payments in sandboxes. Keep that scope tied to the May fraud-factor passage, rather than asserting a current blanket sandbox restriction for all Risk Insights.

May explains numerical factors as comparative charge likelihood for similar values versus the Stripe average. High-risk charges are expected to have some factors above 1 and low-risk charges some below 1. It describes possible changes over time and says a fraud decision can follow from a combination without individually suspicious factors.
conflicts: The summary says Fraud Teams only, no sandbox, and high/low factors as categorical conclusions, and equates low authorization rate with suspicious behavior. Narrow these to the May availability and sandbox evidence, and retain probability wording from both captures.

The dedicated Risk Insights guide says customer ID/IP/card while the November transaction reviews guide says email/IP/card for its linked Related Payments text. Preserve both formulations separately and avoid inferring an exhaustive union or treating customer ID as email.
unresolved_questions: The November capture does not settle current feature/plan/sandbox eligibility for fraud-factor details or whether the review-guide email and dedicated-guide customer ID descriptions reflect different views or editorial drift.

findings: Add the November raw and date the May Fraud Teams and detailed factor/sandbox assertions. Preserve the six-month interface restriction, contextual fraud-factor multipliers, and non-deterministic low-authorization wording.

Retain reciprocal Radar concept and Review and integration checklist routes. Update the concept's undated eligibility/sandbox wording and preserve the separate documented Related Payments matching descriptions.
conflicts: A current answer using categorical eligibility or suspicion overstates the evidence. The linked November Review guide and dedicated Risk Insights guide use different customer identifiers for Related Payments.
source_assessments.reason: Without dated claims, readers may draw unwarranted current product-access and risk conclusions from the older summary. Both captures retain substantial behavioral content and should remain discoverable.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews/risk-insights, source-stripe-radar-risk-insights should cover the November 7 full capture and date the May 10 detail. Both describe Radar evaluating hundreds of factors to score/level a payment and use those results to decide whether to block or mark it for review. A merchant can open Show all insights, and transactions older than the up-to-six-month retention window cannot use the interface (old raw lines 8-13, old raw lines 23-28, new raw lines 9-16). The integrator provides signal values such as email, IP and shipping address to support fuller assessment. The merchant may inspect name/email correspondence, network authorization rate associated with email, billing/shipping/IP geography, and other payments to its own business sharing customer ID, IP or card number. A low authorization rate might indicate suspicious behavior, and common links can help investigate card testing or trial abuse. Neither is an automatic fraud verdict (old raw lines 15-21, old raw lines 51-56, new raw lines 18-28). The current summary captures May's additional factor detail but overstates authorization-rate certainty and does not date its Fraud Teams or sandbox qualifications. November gives no new availability or sandbox assertions (old raw line 8, old raw lines 30-49, new raw lines 9-24).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews/risk-insights, source-stripe-radar-risk-insights needs a dated source_required_update. The separate November Review guide raw/stripe-radar-transaction-reviews-2026-11-07.md at line 52 says email/IP/card instead. Keep the reciprocal stripe-radar concept, dated eligibility/sandbox wording, and transaction review and integration checklist routes.
